Dark Verse #2

Reaper

RuNyx, Maria Adam (Translator)

4.27
115,187 ratings13,366 reviews
Rate this book
Predator a fost doar începutul. Reaper rescrie regulile jocului.

Mai periculos, mai tensionat, mai pasional: Reaper împinge povestea lui Tristan și a Moranei dincolo de orice limită.

Tristan Caine și Morana Vitalio se afundă și mai adânc în lumea întunecată a mafiei. Legătura lor devine tot mai profundă, însă tensiunile dintre ei se amplifică, alimentate de secrete nespuse și de umbrele trecutului.

Află deznodământul unei iubiri născute din ură, crescută în mijlocul mafiei și dusă până la capăt cu sânge, loialitate și atingeri care ard mai tare decât orice trădare.

Ce se întâmplă atunci când vântul de nestăpânit și marea fără sfârșit se ciocnesc în întunericul nopții?

Tristan „Predator” Caine nu era pregătit pentru Morana Vitalio. După o viață trăită sub un jurământ pe care l-a încălcat într-o noapte ploioasă, se trezește sfâșiat între un trecut dureros și un viitor nesigur. Un singur lucru îi este clar: viața ei încă îi aparține.

Pentru Morana, granița dintre dușmani și aliați s-a estompat. Tot ce prețuia s-a năruit, iar necunoscutul o învăluie cu amenințarea lui. Libertatea și viața ei atârnă de un fir de păr, într-un teritoriu unde pericolul pândește la fiecare pas. Și totuși, singura certitudine rămâne: viața lui i-a aparținut dintotdeauna.

Cu douăzeci de ani de istorie care îi leagă, Tristan și Morana pornesc împreună în căutarea adevărului. Însă curând își dau seama că disparițiile misterioase ale fetelor nu sunt decât începutul.

Secretele bine îngropate încep să iasă la lumină.

Piesele de domino încep să cadă.

Iar furtuna e pe cale să se dezlănțuie.

About the author

RuNyx

19 books23.5k followers
RuNyx is a New York Times, USA Today and international bestselling author of romance. Her stories range across subgenres from dark contemporary to gothic to historical to fantasy and more, and are currently being translated into over 10 languages.

Her pen name has a very special meaning to her. When she's not writing, she's reading, traveling, meditating, daydreaming, and most of all, procrastinating.

”i don’t even know who i am.”
a hand fisted in her wet hair and pulled her head back firmly, another wrapping around her throat, demanding her attention.
morana closed her eyes.
”look at me,” he ordered, squeezing her neck once.
the grip tightened, and she opened her eyes, staring at his throat.
”eyes,” the demand found its way through the fog.
slowly, morana looked at him. she found those beautiful, magnificent blue eyes looking at her with anything but hate.
”you are exactly where you’re supposed to be,” he told her, his voice leaving no room for doubts. “i know exactly who you are.”
”who am i?”
”mine.”
morana felt her chin quiver, her eyes burning.
”you are morana. my morana. you’re the woman i killed for and you’re the woman i’d die for. you are mine and you are exactly where you’re supposed to be. don’t ever question that again, do you understand?”
”don’t hate me again.”
his hand flexed on her throat. “do you know why i enjoy holding you like this?”
she shook her head.
”i can feel your life under my hand,” he stated, his eyes burning on hers, his fingers locking her life to him. ”your body, your life, your heart — they’re all mine now. trust me to keep all of them safe.”

➳ 4.5/5 stars

"She was his gravity, his fucking planet, and he was lost without her"

Well, this book picks up right where "The Predator" ends, and to say it was amazing would be an understatement. I thoroughly enjoyed the story and the characters, but the writing style just wasn’t my type. And only because of that, I'm not giving it a full 5 stars.

In this book, Tristan and Morana are on a quest to unmask the mysterious "Reaper" behind all the chaos. Alongside this thrilling pursuit, their love story unfolds beautifully. While the tension between them was palpable in the first book, it skyrockets in this one. I adored how they fiercely stood up for each other and always had each other's backs. The chemistry between them was simply electric.

╰┈➤ Tristan Caine

This man needs to be protected at all costs. Witnessing his transformation from an emotionally guarded individual to someone who is making an effort to be vulnerable was truly unexpected. While men in love can do all sorts of things, seeing him change himself for the person he loves is the most profound of all. It's a testament to the depth of his feelings and the strength of their bond.

I have never encountered a character quite like Tristan. Quiet yet profoundly supportive, he goes above and beyond for this woman – caring for her, protecting her fiercely, cooking for her, and even washing her hair. While these actions might seem like the bare minimum, they feel extraordinary coming from Tristan. The character development in this book was incredibly well-crafted. Opening up his personal space and being vulnerable wasn't easy for him, yet he is willing to do everything for her. Moreover, he is never once intimidated by her intelligence; on the contrary, he finds it deeply attractive, which is a rare and refreshing trait even in real life.

"But I never, ever want you to not walk into a room and know that every part of me, fucked up man and the lost boy, belong to you."


╰┈➤ Morana Vitalio

At this point, I'm almost at a loss for words to describe this extraordinary woman. She embodies perfection in every sense. Intelligent, well-spoken, bold, and fiercely independent – she has it all. Yet, what truly stood out in this book was her immense courage. Despite grappling with her own trauma, she never once considered giving up on Tristan or their relationship. Instead, she poured her heart into making it work, often taking the lead and showing remarkable strength and commitment. Her unwavering dedication and efforts to nurture their bond make her an exceptional character, truly deserving of admiration.

Her fearlessness in speaking her mind was truly awe-inspiring. I mean, who else would have the guts to stand up to a mafia boss like Lorenzo Maroni and demand accountability for his despicable actions? She's a force to be reckoned with, a true embodiment of strength and integrity. I find myself at a loss for words when it comes to describing her – she's simply the complete package. Needless to say, I'm eagerly anticipating delving deeper into her character in the other books.

"I'm not a victim. I'm vengeance, Mark my words, Mr. Maroni. I am going to make you pay - for every single scar you've put on Tristan; for every little hurt you inflicted on Dante; for banishing Amara from her home. And for all the girls who went missing."


╰┈➤ Tristan and Morana

Their relationship in this book was truly impressive. Despite my initial doubts, it exceeded my expectations. The progression felt genuine and well-paced, allowing the characters to build trust in each other naturally. What stood out to me was the authenticity in their interactions, as both characters made sincere efforts to understand and support one another. It was a refreshing portrayal of a developing bond that felt both relatable and heartfelt.

Tristan's decision to tattoo Morana's name on his ring finger, despite the obstacles preventing their marriage, spoke volumes about the depth of their connection. It was a gesture that resonated deeply, reflecting the complex emotions they shared, shaped by their turbulent pasts. Their story is one of profound significance, leaving an enduring imprint on my heart. I am certain that their characters will continue to occupy my thoughts long after I've turned the final page of their book.

"Your body, your life, your heart – they’re all mine now. Trust me to keep all of them safe.”

➳ Overall, if you're in need of a riveting read that will hold your attention from beginning to end, this book is your perfect pick. Enjoyy! 🫶🏻

"And then his voice, the voice of whiskey and sin, spoke in death."

Oh my god. This book was so hard to read because you have one Tristan Caine and one Morana vitalio who are so hot and their tension explodes everything so it was very hard to read without getting sucked in WHICH I GOT and then was left wanting more as it ended.. and like the way the story revolves around them and weaves its path along the way is so beautiful. The journey that these two book alone take us on are so well written and so fun to read. I honestly dont know which book I like more!! it switches between this and the emperor. Last time it was this soo lets see what book I like more this time.

"She was his gravity, his fucking planet, and he was lost without her."

Again, I loved Runyx's storytelling in this book. It was just pure class. The way she was able show affection and emotions from Tristan' and Moranas scenes were so perfectly done and again I liked how she kept a balance between the romance and the plot. She really mad eme feel about the character without giving everything about the book to them and honestly I applaud her for the pacing becuase it's so fast but it's also not rushed?? so it is so fun to read and her writing itself is so fun. I think I have read it so much that the repetitive nature of this book didn bother me as it does most of the people. One more thing about these books that I like are how they get more darker with each book (we are not counting the finisher)

"If you burned as I burn with the need to claim you. That I wasn’t alone in the fire."

There were no new tropes to be honest but some prominent ones were:
Who did this to you?,
When he gets sick and she takes care of him
When she gets sick and he takes care of her.
Found family
Angst
Spice
Lots of staring

"You are exactly where you were supposed to be,” he told her, his voice leaving no room for doubts. “I know exactly who you are.” “Who am I?” “Mine."

Tristan, I still love this blue eyed cutie who calls himself the predator and hunts people down but is downbad for Morana. I loved how he was with Morana how he cared for her and how he showed affections by his actions and not only by his words. I actually really want hear his voice now (I still dont know why this series doesnt have an audiobook) because I'm so intrigued to see what whiskey and sin actually sounds like. We were robbed of more bike scenes, that is one of my mainc omplaint becuase there was one scene in the predator that I liked sooo much, the one where Morana lifts her hands up and screams in joy as she sits behind Tristan remains as one of my favourites for sure. His story actually broke my heart and his quest to find his sister broke it even further.

"I’m not a victim. I’m vengeance."

Morana, this book proved that 'wildcat' is among one of the best female leads written. How she dealt with Tristan and gave him time and space was really what made me love her even more than I thought was possible. She was so nice to him and her friendship with Amara really blossomed too but I wish we got more of there scenes. What I love the most is how close Dante and Morana became. Like literally one of the cutest found family moments here. There was a part of this book that made me appreciate Moranas firendship with Amara and her contribution to the plot as well. I think I love it when FMC's delivered and Morana for me delivered. Also, I felt so sad for Morana by the end of this book, she deserves everything!!

"You,” she whispered to the space between them, “Tristan Caine, are a beautiful, beautiful man. And my heart beats for you."

Romance, there was communication which was imo dealt with in a really good way between both the characters. I loved the intense staring, the overall vibe and the hotness the Tristan snd Morana eluded had me sweating. Everything that they said to each other, every jab, every snarky remark had me bouncing off the walls. There's a reasonw hy they're the best couple and why they have the highest rated book and like come on!! no one compares to them and the spice was honestly so very spicy even more than the first book but still balanced overall. Tristan and Morana had me 🧎 🙏 I love them so much. The epilogue was everything I loved it. I honestly want so much more from them in the syndicator you dont even know.

"He wanted to tell her that love was too tame a word for everything that happened inside him where she was concerned. She had shifted him, realigned him from the inside out. Like a planet that suddenly pulls a moon into its orbit, she had bound him to her, given him direction for longer than she knew, gave him purpose to exist."

The plot and the action scenes along with the world building in this book was top notch. One of the best out there. The action sequences were so good and yk the feeling of dread when you feel that something might happen to a character you love? Yeah that happened alot here. Despite having alot if action sequences and stunts my favourite would be Tristan meeting Morana inside her house from the predator. The last half of this book was dropping twists after twists. My jaw was on the floor, and it refused to go back up. The end hurt me so much but overall it was amazing!!

"I'm so in love with you, caveman."
"You can't take that back."

Finally, Dante and Amara the side characters were as always so much fun to read about and Im loving their book even more. The only thing I wanted in this book were povs from Tristan's side like got from Dantes in the emperor.
_
cant believe this is the only TristanMorana book until the last one 🥺 Idk whether to savor or devour this (devour 🙂‍↕️) Reread#2 😝

”you’re the girl I killed for and you’re the woman I’d die for.”


there are times when you aren’t prepared for a book. not prepared enough for an agonizing read that wrecks your soul in tatters and then stitches the fragments back together. not prepared to fall for morally questionable but attaching characters, questing for the forgiveness drown in their past and present mistakes. not enough prepared to be captured between the pages of a new world ruled by a gripping and masterminding plot, seeking for answers by eroding the blurred barrier between the past and present lies. I was taken aback by Morana and Tristan's story. the two books dedicated to their epic telling exceeded my expectations in terms of depth, scheming, and brain.

”His demons dance with mine,” she murmured softly, the truth of that statement seeping into her pores.”


I can be easily seduced by well-written books and bewitched under the spell of their writing. & it’s precisely what occurred with this book and the previous one. i was enchanted by RuNyx’s melodic and poignant plume from the very first words of 'The Predator'. it has such an eloquent voice that melancholically and ironically sang with the ruthless universe the author moulded in the vicinity of 'The Dark Verse Series'. every word had a herd of stumbling meanings behind it. every cryptic quote and phrasing mirrored one too many poetic significances.

” And he had. Even before she had asked him to make a choice, he already had. Even before he knew that she knew, he had wanted to protect her. Even before she had exposed herself to him the way she had, he had wanted her.”


Tristan and Morana. Morana and Tristan. both of them were wounded souls whose pasts and fates were strangely and cruelly entangled. every tiny, twisted, and dark parcel of one of them was in symbiosis with the second one. while the dynamic between them was not typical, it was a masterpiece of enemies to lovers’ arc. it started with them as morbid rivals; their animosity and hatred suffocatingly intense. their pursuit to harm or kill each other untempered.

”Some days, he felt like he would
explode with the emotions she pulled from his once-dead heart.”


but it eventually converged with them being an entity; their empathy and hurt for each other, their love and devotion, their acceptance and approval of one another. In every sense of the word, they perfectly completed each other. ❤️‍🩹

”Morana held him through the pain, her own eyes tearing up as he cried in her arms.”
this scene broke me.

Wayyyy better than the first book. I swear I had the time of my life with this one.

My issues with the first book was that the second half was super underwhelming and this one was the exact opposite. The second half here was so action packed, chemistry packed and the plot twist towards the end took it all up a notch. There was still a lot of repetition when it came to "whiskey and sin voice" but having an idea about it beforehand helped. The book had me so immersed that am willing to ignore it this time around... and that's saying something👀

Tristan and Morana have my heart. These two are so perfect for each other, especially Morana who is so patient with him. She gives him space, she lets him be vulnerable and open, never forcing, never controlling and it's so admirable to me. Tristan... My man truly is whiskey and sin (yeah yeah, I know I caved in.. Besides I read it so many times, am used to it now.) I absolutely LOVED him in this one. An underrated thing about him? He doesn't talk rubbish. He doesn't babble. He just talks enough, and it's so meaningful. Basically, he's not one to eat your head. He was so much more in this one. The man radiates power, charm and sex.. and he knows it 👀 *sigh* Why is he fictional 😭

Their relationship had so much depth in this one. They're so much more than just spice tbh. The way they're loyal to each other and the way they understand each other is EVERYTHING!! I love a relationship without any toxicity, there was no miscommunication, just open, honest talks and a whole lotta trust. The way they can just communicate with each other by their expressions and body language 🤌🤌

Am definitely intrigued by the world created by RuNyx and what role the Syndicate has to play in the future. The ending was perfect imo and especially that epilogue 🥺🥺 Also, Dante baby am coming for you and Amara soon. I really hope he doesn't talk in whiskey and sin tho.

Whiskey and sin voice count- Innumerable.

“She was his gravity, his fucking planet, and he was lost without her.”


Tristan and Morana will never be out of my system. The Reaper is a masterpiece and one of the best books I have ever read in my life. I felt an undeniable connection to this book, its characters, and their love story, and my love for Tristan and Morana has only ignited into a fiery blaze after reading the next part of their journey. This is, without a doubt, RuNyx’s best work, and I will never deny this fact in the future.

“They were similar - she and him. Two sides of the same coin, two ends of the same string.”


The Reaper follows the epic and unforgettable love story of Tristan and Morana, continuing the mind-blowing, interconnected plotline of the Dark Verse series after the cliffhanger at the end of the previous book. It picks up right where The Predator ended, but this time, it’s more thrilling, more gory, more mysterious, more dark—more EPIC. The past and present unravel alongside secrets and lies that have been blurred and buried for decades by The Syndicate, and RuNyx masterfully handles every arc of the story.

Morana Vitalio is a force to be reckoned with. She’s fire—untamed and fierce. Her perseverance, boldness, protectiveness, and patience speak volumes about what an incredible and exceptional woman she is. Morana is perfection in every sense. I admire her bravery and inner strength—the way she fights for and protects the people she loves, how she’s always the first to step forward, ready to be helpful and resourceful when needed. She is THE woman. A formidable force. An unapologetic queen with the intelligence to destroy everything in her path. A courageous and brave woman who can crumble even the strongest, most impenetrable walls built around the most dangerous man in their world. I love how she never stopped loving Tristan—how, despite her trauma and heartache, she still finds joy in the little things, how she consistently pours her love, care, and patience into building a relationship with a man who once swore to kill her. That kind of love is rare.

“I’m not a victim. I’m vengeance, Mark my words, Mr. Maroni. I am going to make you pay - for every single scar you’ve put on Tristan; for every little hurt you inflicted on Dante; for banishing Amara from her home. And for all the girls who went missing.”


Tristan Caine is a man who needs to be protected at all costs. A boy who was broken beyond repair by the very people who were supposed to protect and love him. A weapon trained to kill. A man with a singular purpose—to end the girl who unknowingly set his life on its dark trajectory. Tristan in The Predator was dangerous and cruel, but Tristan in The Reaper is a man who is learning and trying. Learning to show emotions. Learning to be vulnerable. Learning what it means to have someone see him—not as the monster the world believes him to be, but as the man Morana knows he is. It was deeply emotional to witness him unveiling his feelings, lowering his defenses, and letting Morana in. He was so soft in this book. So thoughtful. Letting Morana take care of him, letting himself feel everything he tried to bury for years—his obsession, his protectiveness, his love for her. I love how he is trying. His character development is phenomenal. He is sharing everything with her—his space, his thoughts, his vulnerability, his emotions, his past, and his future.

“They will die a thousand deaths,” he murmured, “before they ever touch a single hair on your head again.”


Tristan and Morana are intrinsically tied to each other—two souls forged in darkness yet drawn together by something deeper than fate. She is his reason to live and breathe—his kryptonite, his weakness, his strength, his everything. Witnessing their love blossom into something more than just friendship, more than just healing, was an honor, to be honest. Their relationship development in this book was perfectly executed. They let each other in—not just into their lives but into their pasts, offering one another their rawest truths and deepest vulnerabilities. Together, they peeled back the carefully guarded layers around their hearts, healing each other in ways neither of them thought possible.

“You, Tristan Caine, are a beautiful, beautiful man. And my heart beats for you.”


Their love story is a testament to the transformative power of trust and honesty. They built something real—a bond that transcended pain and tragedy, a semblance of happiness in a world steeped in darkness. Tristan and Morana built their relationship on a foundation of trust and honesty, allowing them to break free from the walls they had spent years constructing. Watching Tristan open up to Morana, allowing her to understand him, to hold him, to heal him, to love him unconditionally, was both emotionally profound and utterly captivating.

“You might have been born with another name but you are Morana. My Morana. You’re the girl I killed for and you’re the woman I’d die for. You are mine and you are exactly where you’re supposed to be. Don’t ever question that again, do you understand?”


There’s no denying how gorgeous and magnificent RuNyx’s writing and prose are. I get lost in her stories every time, and this one is no different. The way she weaves a storyline filled with allegorical metaphors, vivid imagery, deeply complex and well-developed characters, and love stories that make you feel an entire spectrum of emotions is breathtaking. This book masterfully showcased the soft, wholesome, fierce, and vulnerable sides of both Tristan and Morana, interwoven with the broken pieces of their pasts. Every moment, every stolen glance, every whispered confession built a love story that was as hauntingly real as it was breathtakingly beautiful.

This series has consumed my thoughts and my life. Tristan and Morana have touched my heart, my soul, in an irrevocable way, and I will always carry them with me.

This book is a continuation to the first book. Tristan and Morana are the ultimate power couple. Watching them hunt down the Reaper while navigating their own evolving relationship was incredible. The slow-burn tension from the first book finally reaches a breaking point, and the payoff is worth it, trust. Their loyalty is what really got me. They are so protective of each other. I loved their fierce loyalty and the way they constantly showed up for each other. Their chemistry is pure electricity!

✮⋆˙ 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐚 𝐕𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐨
“You,” she whispered to the space between them, “Tristan Caine, are a beautiful, beautiful man. And my heart beats for you.”

I honestly just want to be like Morana. She is the definition of a 'wildcat'- bold, intelligent and unapologetically herself. The emotional maturity she showed while giving Tristan space was beautiful and her courage never wavered. I was especially moved by the found-family moments she shared with Dante and Amara. My heart absolutely broke for her at the end of the series. After everything she went through, she deserved a much happier ending.

✮⋆˙ 𝐓𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧 𝐂𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐞
“You might have been born with another name but you are Morana. My Morana. You’re the girl I killed for and you’re the woman I’d die for... you are exactly where you’re supposed to be. Don’t ever question that again, do you understand?”

There is just something about Tristan Caine. He is a lethal hunter yet he is the ultimate softie for Morana. Their dynamic is everything, his actions always speak louder than words. especially how he chooses to show his love through acts of service and fierce protection. His journey to find his sister was gut-wrenching and watching him slowly lower his guard was a great character growth. It is also so rare and refreshing to see a male lead who is genuinely captivated by a woman’s brilliance rather than threatened by it. He truly is one of a kind.

"In the arms of the most dangerous man she knew, she felt the safest she had ever been."


The moment Tristan tattooed Morana’s name on his ring finger moved me to tears. Even without a formal marriage, that gesture proved their bond is unbreakable. Their connection is so layered and intense. This story truly stayed with me.

The "romance" is basically just Morona making assumptions. He doesn't want her dead, so now they're suddenly boyfriend and girlfriend. Bestie, don't you think that one requires a conversation? And it all felt so awkward with her apparently being the queen of relationships and going off about "you know we're in a committed relationship right?".
Well this is the first I am hearing about it.

I know her making assumptions is supposed to be seen as caring, a "she knows him better than anybody else"-type thing, but the fact is it just reads very condescending.
"Expecting him to understand emotional nuances and express them would be wrong"
"She doubted he even realized that he loved her" He is his own person. Not giving him space to communicate and instead making assumptions is wrong.

And him testing her? It gave me the biggest ick and I couldn't get into it at all after that.

I stand by Morona being an unlikeable character, and not in a good way. No wonder she never had any friends(sorry too far?) She is so full of herself. Why is she stating she is a genius every five seconds, but does nothing to actually live up to that. If you're gonna build a character that is very proud of her intellect, I expect her intelligence be a key part to solve the mystery and her being knee deep in the investigation. Instead she was just a pawn for everybody else.
I did like her in her battles with Mr. Maroni, but then when she didn't do any of the revenge she promised even that just feels phoney and like she's boosting her own skills(but having none).

Although it's lighthearted, her username being "Nerdy Tech Goddess" tells me everything I need to know about her. She has so many cringe moments that made me want to drop this book in the nearest ocean.
"Morana mentally patted herself on the back for a blowjob well done. The gods of oral would be proud" I nearly cried reading that. And idk about you, but personally I won't forgive her for being a bad friend to Amara.

Even though I was disappointed with how it developed I did enjoy myself a lot for the first half.
I enjoyed Tristans protectiveness, how the plot deepened, Dante and Moranas kinship, Zia.
The writing didn't seem as painful as well - however, there were definitely moments where the writing did take me out of the story. Like a "Whiskey and Sin" one or ten times too much.

I know I will enjoy Amara & Dantes story more, but right now I desperately need a break from this writing or I will actually go insane.

sorry for the messy and ranty review, it was cathartic getting all of this out though ngl

I am usually not a fan of reading different books about the same couple and I get it that the 1st book didn't really shed any light onto their relationship so, this book was a necessary addition. But, it felt unnecessarily long to me. When I started this book and got to a good chunk of 30%, the slump got to me and I stopped reading for nearly 17 days even after being done with my exams. There were some paras describing Tristan's house by the lake a handful times which really felt like a drag on. Another being the constant repetition of phrases like "whiskey and sin spoke", "whiskey and sin entered the room", "the predator did so and so". There wasn't really anything concrete happening for a good part of the book.

Coming to the twist, I guessed it way before I began this book. It felt stupid and was just added to preserve the 'shock' value and failed for me. And the foremost issue being the time limit dedicated to the mystery, how come you concluded it and few deaths in 2 fucking pages? When the mystery was the focal point of the book aside from their relationship. I was close to dropping this book many times but I didn't want to betray my babies.

This was overall a 3.5 read, had to increase the rating because-

➞ Men crying does it for me.

➞ I liked the way Runyx orchestrated the ending by relating things to how they began in book 1.

➞ Tristan and Morana because there's nothing wrong with them.

I'm looking forward to DanteAmara and I'm already so fiercely protective of Amara. I will def be needing a break from the series for a while, might as well switch genres for the time being.

“You,Tristan Caine, are a beautiful, beautiful man. And my heart beats for you.”
I feel this quote sums up how I feel. I absolutely love Tristan Caine and the man that he is! This man will kill for her, make her breakfast, give her chocolate, wash her hair, and die for her. PLEASE GIVE ME THIS MAN! I feel he has ruined me but in such a good way because I don't know if any other book boyfriend can match up to him, even though I am really hoping Dante does the same.
"He would be her ruin. And she would ruin him right back."
This book starts off right where the first one left off. I thoroughly enjoyed the first book but when I say I loved this one, I mean I LOVED this one. The little things that fell short for me in the first book, the author came back and hit it out of the park with this one. The chapters were shorter and this one I felt was a lot more plot driven. You think you are addicted to a book until you read the next one and it is even more addicting!🤣 I wanted more of Amara but I know she has her own books coming up so it didn't take away from this one at all. By the end of it I felt so many emotions and was so in love with it I just wanted to scream!!!

જ⁀➴TRISTAN & MORANA
These two are literally perfect for each other. Nobody else could handle Tristan Caine. Morana is intelligent yet she spits fire and that is just what he needs. Tristan is a deadly predator that protects her to the end of the world and thats what she needs. They are two halfs that make each other whole and watching their development is the intoxicating ride that it was. Runyx did an amazing job at staying true to Tristan's character. For a man of very few words she found ways to show how he cares through his actions. Morana has all the patience in the world for this man and that is what makes them so special. She doesn't try to "fix" him, she just loves him for who he is. Her heart breaks for him and yet she is strong for him, she loves him and gives him the space he needs. They are each other's oxygen in a world of suffocation. Omg i could go on forever and I would never do them justice. I can't not think of a single fictional couple that has had me in such a chokehold as these two.
“I will tell you this—I don’t want to fix him. I want to fix me. And he’s the only thing that seems to be working. His demons dance with mine”

જ⁀➴DANTE
Dante is the cool and collected opposite of Tristan. He is the brother and friend that Tristan and Morana need. He makes me laugh and he is always there to defend and protect those he love. I can't wait to read his story and learn more about him and the way his mind works. Dante I beg that you ruin me the way that Tristan has!

જ⁀➴FAVORITE QUOTES
"The man holding her was darkness. He was comfortable in the dark, one with the dark, owned the dark. And as long as he held her the way he did, safe in his arms, that dark was hers. It belonged to her. She was comfortable in it, safe in it, one with it."
“If you burned as I burn with the need to claim you. That I wasn’t alone in the fire.”
"You’re the girl I killed for and you’re the woman I’d die for. You are mine and you are exactly where you’re supposed to be. Don’t ever question that again, do you understand?”
"She had shifted him, realigned him from the inside out. Like a planet that suddenly pulls a moon into its orbit, she had bound him to her, given him direction for longer than she knew, gave him purpose to exist. She was his gravity, his fucking planet, and he was lost without her."

REDEMPTION!!!!! I am so glad I listened to all my besties that told me to hang in there bc this book was FIRE!

The follow-up to The Predator starts right where we left Morana and Tristan. Now they are on a mission to find out what happened to the codes and the mystery surrounding the missing girls while surrounded by enemies and figuring out how their relationship will work in this volatile world of crime.

I loved how we got so much more information about Tristan in this book, he became a real person instead of just an idea and it was really well done. His relationship with Morana was so sweet and so many times I was saying awwww out loud! The way Morana just knows what he can and can't give and accepts him completely was really beautiful.
I also really, really love Dante and the friendship he has with Morana. I am so curious about his story and am really looking forward to reading it.

That last 20 percent though!!!! 🤯🤯🤯 Blew my mind, never saw that coming and the way everything played out was AMAZING!! Morana is a QUEEN!

The writing is still a little goofy sometimes with all the stream of consciousness monologuing but since I had managed my expectations for this from the previous book I didn't mind it so much. So thks again to my besties who encouraged to me to hang in there bc it was totally worth it and YOU WERE ALL RIGHT!!!
